topic: Yeonmal jeongsan (연말정산), Korea's year-end tax settlement for salaried workers. Employer withholds income tax monthly by the simplified withholding table, then settles the real amount early the next year; most employees never file their own return. NTS simplified service (간소화 서비스) opened 2026-01-15 with 45 types of deduction data. Card deduction: only spending above 25% of gross salary counts; credit card 15%, debit card/cash receipts 30% (Restriction of Special Taxation Act art. 126-2). Difference paid or charged with February/March pay. 2024 income (NTS statistics, reported 2025-12-23): 21.08M filers, 14.23M refunded avg ₩893,000, 3.77M paid extra avg ₩1.17M, 6.84M (32.4%) owed zero tax. Nickname '13th-month salary' (13월의 월급). No other-country comparison.
title: In Korea, January Brings a 13th Paycheck

slides.headline: In Korea, January brings a **13th paycheck.**
slides.note: Or a bill. It depends on your receipts.

slides.headline: Your company **does your taxes**
slides.body: Most office workers in Korea never file a tax return. Every month, the company takes tax out of your pay using a set table. Early the next year, it checks the real number.

slides.headline: It's called **yeonmal jeongsan**
slides.body: It means "year-end settlement." The tax taken from your pay is compared with the tax you actually owe. Too much taken? You get it back. Too little? You pay the rest.

slides.headline: The receipts **find you**
slides.body: In mid-January, the National Tax Service opens your records online: card spending, hospital bills, school fees, insurance, donations. 45 kinds of data, most of it already filled in.

slides.headline: Your cards **count**
slides.body: Card spending above 25% of your yearly salary lowers your taxable income. Credit cards count at 15%, debit cards and cash receipts at 30%. That's why many people switch cards once they pass the line.

slides.headline: Settled with **February pay**
slides.body: You check the records, add anything missing, and hand it to your company. The money comes back, or comes out, with your February or March pay.

slides.headline: average **refund**
slides.body: 14.23 million workers got money back for 2024. Another 3.77 million paid more, about ₩1.17 million each.

slides.headline: One in three **pays nothing**
slides.body: After all deductions, 6.84 million workers, 32.4% of everyone who settled, owed no income tax at all for 2024.

slides.headline: That's why **November** matters
slides.body: Spending up to December 31 still counts. So now is when people plan: which card to use, what to donate, which bills to pay before the year ends.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.

caption:
In Korea, most office workers never file a tax return. The company does it, and every January the numbers get checked again.

About 14 million workers got money back for 2024, ₩893,000 on average. Koreans call it the "13th-month salary."

Do you file your own taxes where you live?
reply: Not everyone wins. 3.77 million workers had to pay more for 2024, about ₩1.17 million each, usually because too little tax was taken during the year. That's why some people call January the "13th-month salary" and others call it the "13th-month bomb." Which one would you get?
fact_check: 1장·캡션: '13월의 월급' 별칭 — 언론 통용 표현(이데일리·세계일보 2026-10, 네이트뉴스 2025-12-23).
2·3장: 회사가 매월 간이세액표로 원천징수, 다음 해 초 연말정산 — 소득세법 원천징수·연말정산 규정, 국세청 연말정산 안내. 근로소득만 있으면 종합소득세 신고 불필요.
4장: 2026-01-15 간소화 서비스 개통, 공제자료 45종 — 국세청 공지 2026-01-14(nts.go.kr), 머니투데이 2026-01-14. '1월 중순'으로 표현.
5장: 총급여 25% 초과분만 공제, 신용카드 15%·체크카드·현금영수증 30% — 조세특례제한법 제126조의2. 카드 바꾸기는 일반 절세 요령으로 'many people' 표현.
6장: 회사 제출 후 2~3월 급여에서 환급·추징 — 국세청 안내(원천징수 신고 3월 10일).
7장·reply: 2024년 귀속 환급 1,423만 명 평균 89만3천 원, 추가 납부 377만 명 평균 117만 원 — 국세통계(네이트뉴스 2025-12-23). 다른 집계(국회 제출, 1,485만 명·84만7천 원)도 있어 국세통계 기준으로 통일.
8장: 결정세액 0인 면세자 684만 명, 32.4% — 같은 국세통계 보도.
9장: 12월 31일 지출까지 해당 연도 공제 — 연말정산 대상 기간(1/1~12/31).
